title: The Lost Provision
premise: Elodie Marchetti has spent a decade outrunning their father's shadow and the debts he left behind, digging where no one looks and leaving before anyone asks questions. When dying prospector Amos Vane trades them a map to a lost supply cache hidden in the Sawtooth Range—for a promise that his granddaughter will be told the truth—Elodie inherits both the treasure and the trouble it carries: a mining consortium's expired concession claim, a rival crew, and a race against the first snows. Crossing the range with Amos's granddaughter, Mara, Elodie must choose between selling the cache and vanishing again, or honoring a promise that could finally cost them everything. In the end, Elodie surrenders the map's location to the land itself, keeping only the truth for Mara—and discovering that staying was the one thing worth stopping for.
about_author: Jude Sterling is the pen name of a former field surveyor who spent six seasons in remote mountain ranges before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who measure their lives in miles and regret.

chapters.title: Dust on the Shovel
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Working a dead-end claim in a border town, Elodie is recognized by a man from their father's old expedition and flees mid-dig, abandoning tools and a week's wages. The beat establishes restlessness as survival instinct—and the loneliness underneath it.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In a mining-camp saloon, dying prospector Amos Vane offers Elodie a hand-drawn map to a lost 1890s provision cache in exchange for a promise: tell his estranged granddaughter the truth of how he lost her family's stake. Elodie accepts, telling themselves it's just another job.

chapters.title: What the Map Costs
chapters.summary: Mara Vane's POV. Elodie finds Mara working a river ferry and delivers Amos's message; Mara, furious at the grandfather who abandoned her mother, demands to come along—not for closure, she says, but for her half of whatever's there. First friction, grudging alliance.

chapters.title: Concession
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In the last supply town, Elodie discovers the Halvard Consortium holds an expiring permit covering the entire range—and their survey crews are already hunting the same cache using Amos's stolen field notes. The clock starts: cross before the snows, ahead of the crews.

chapters.title: The Low Pass
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The pair takes a disused trail through the low pass; a rockslide nearly kills Mara, and Elodie's quick, practiced rescue reveals how many times they've run from collapsing ground. Trust begins to form over a fire neither wanted to light.

chapters.title: Ghost Camp
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They shelter in an abandoned expedition camp—Elodie's father's camp, from the trip that ended him. Forced to tell Mara the story, Elodie confronts why they never stop moving: staying is where people die. Mara challenges that arithmetic.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The consortium crew catches up; in a sudden storm above treeline, both parties are trapped in the same cave overnight. Elodie and the crew leader, Reyes, trade truths about what the cache actually is—and what each would burn down to get it.

chapters.title: The Provision House
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They reach the cache first: not gold but a sealed provision house—tools, seed stock, deeds, and letters proving Amos's family was cheated of their legal claim. The inheritance isn't wealth; it's standing. Reyes arrives with guns drawn as the snows begin in earnest.

chapters.title: Held Ground
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Climax. Besieged in the provision house through a two-day blizzard, Mara stakes her claim on the deeds while Elodie, offered escape by Reyes, chooses to stay—the thing they've never done. The storm breaks; the consortium, facing expired permits and witnesses, withdraws.

chapters.title: First Light on the Range
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Thaw. Mara files the claim under her grandfather's restored name; Elodie, for the first time, doesn't leave—signing on as the dig's archaeologist instead of its ghost. The promise kept becomes a home found. Quiet resolution: survival was never the prize; staying was.
